advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm it is intended that fetch-secrets (and thus SSM reachability) now gates EVERY bot source redeploy, not only secrets-path changes; if not, gate the refresh on `changed "$SECRETS_PATHS"` (or tolerate SSM-unchanged failures).
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh reads SSM via IMDSv2 + aws ssm get-parameter (infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:35-58); any read failure exits 1, so a transient SSM/IMDS outage now aborts a pure-source deploy that formerly had no SSM step
Comment at autodeploy.sh:206-207 only notes 'no SSM-quota regression' and does not acknowledge that a transient SSM outage now blocks a code-only redeploy
advisory.finding: fetch-secrets.sh now runs on EVERY review-bot redeploy (the block fires on BOT_PATHS OR SECRETS_PATHS), so a pure source-only change (e.g. src/rebar/) that previously deployed with no SSM dependency now aborts on any transient SSM/IMDS failure. This newly couples all bot source deploys to SSM reachability — a behavior change broader than the 'secrets reached the box' fix; the inline comment only frames the cost as SSM-quota, not as a new failure mode blocking previously-independent source deploys.
scenarios: A src/rebar/ code fix is merged during a brief SSM/IMDS blip; deploy aborts + records backoff even though secrets were unchanged and the prior deploy path required no SSM access.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the failure test meaningful (e.g. stub that partially writes .env before exit 1, or drive the real fetch-secrets fail-fast path) so .env-preservation is actually exercised.
evidence: The stub never opens .env, so no code path under test could mutate it — the assertion passes even if autodeploy did nothing

test stub never writes .env: `fs.write_text(f'#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo fetch-secrets >> "{marker}"
exit {exit_code}
')` (test_autodeploy_fetch_secrets.py:125)
autodeploy invokes but never itself writes .env — only the invoked fetch-secrets.sh does (autodeploy.sh:208)
Inverted-trace: were autodeploy to proceed past the failed fetch-secrets, .env would still equal 'PREEXISTING=1\n', so the assertion would still pass — it does not catch the abort-failure regression
advisory.finding: The failure test asserts `env_file.read_text() == 'PREEXISTING=1\n'` to prove autodeploy leaves .env intact on failure, but the fetch-secrets stub used is `echo fetch-secrets >> marker; exit 1` — it never writes .env, so the assertion is trivially true regardless of autodeploy's behavior. It verifies the stub, not that autodeploy (or the real fetch-secrets atomic-write) preserves .env; the .env-preservation guarantee is therefore not actually exercised.
merged_from: The `.env left intact on failure` assertion is inert and cannot detect the regression it purports to guard. autodeploy.sh never writes .env itself (only fetch-secrets.sh does), and the test's fetch-secrets stub echoes a marker then exits without touching .env — so the assertion `env_file.read_text() == 'PREEXISTING=1\n'` holds even if autodeploy wrongly continued past the failed fetch-secrets. It adds no regression-detection power beyond the (valid) build/up-absent and backoff assertions.
scenarios: A future regression where autodeploy or fetch-secrets truncates .env before failing would not be caught by this test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving a BOT_PATHS-only change (e.g. git diff reports src/rebar/ changed) that asserts fetch-secrets still runs before `compose up`, and that a fetch-secrets failure aborts fail-safe on that path too.
evidence: fetch-secrets re-run + fail-safe abort live inside this shared block (autodeploy.sh:208-211), so they now apply to BOT_PATHS-only deploys too
test git stub reports change ONLY for a SECRETS_PATH: `case "$*" in *fetch-secrets.sh*) echo "infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh"` (test_autodeploy_fetch_secrets.py:74)
ABSENCE: search of tests/scripts for BOT_PATHS / compose-up found no test driving a BOT_PATHS-only change through the fetch-secrets refresh
advisory.finding: No test exercises the BOT_PATHS-triggered redeploy path now that it also re-runs fetch-secrets before `compose up`. This change makes EVERY bot redeploy (including the pre-existing source-only BOT_PATHS case) run fetch-secrets and abort fail-safe on its failure — a behavior change for the BOT_PATHS path — yet both new tests drive only the SECRETS_PATHS branch (git stub reports only infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh changed). A regression that scoped the fetch-secrets refresh to only the secrets-source sub-case, or broke it on the common source-deploy path, would go undetected.
